entities.name: Abd al-Aziz ibn Shu'ayb
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Shuʿayb ibn ʿUmar al-Qurṭubī al-Ballūṭī, known as Kouroupas in the Byzantine sources, was the tenth and last Emir of Crete, ruling from 949 to the Byzantine reconquest of the island in 961.

This Emir played a crucial role in the Byzantine- Arab relations in Crete, navigating the complex web of interests between the Eastern Roman Empire and the Islamic Caliphate.

The Byzantine reconquest of Crete in 961 marked the beginning of a new era of Christian rule on the island, which had previously been under Muslim control for nearly a century.

Abd al-Aziz's legacy extends beyond his tenure as Emir, as it contributed to the broader historical context of the Mediterranean world during the 10th century.

The discovery of the Kouroupas archive in the 20th century provided valuable insights into the life and reign of this significant figure, shedding light on the administrative and cultural practices of the Byzantine and Arab rulers of Crete.
